articles.title: Israeli attacks across Gaza kill two people, hit hospital supply warehouse
articles.summary: Gaza’s Health Ministry reports rising casualties amid escalated Israeli attacks, with victims trapped under rubble.
articles.body:
Several people have been wounded in an Israeli strike on a medical warehouse inside a hospital compound in central Gaza, while separate attacks killed two people elsewhere in the Strip.

The Israeli drone strike targeted a tent used as a medical supply warehouse inside the Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital complex in Deir el-Balah on Saturday, injuring three people, the hospital’s director said.

The Israeli military confirmed it hit a target within the compound of Al-Aqsa Hospital, claiming without evidence that a Hamas commander was struck.

Separately, another Israeli drone struck a bike in Gaza City’s Tal al-Hawa neighbourhood. The Palestinian Wafa news agency reported that at least one person was killed and two injured in that attack. The casualties were taken to al-Quds Field Hospital.

In a separate attack earlier in the day, one person was killed by Israeli gunfire in the village of al-Musaddar, east of Deir el-Balah.

An Israeli quadcopter also dropped an explosive device in the vicinity of Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza, according to hospital officials.

Israel has escalated its attacks across the Gaza Strip in recent days despite the so-called “ceasefire”.

Gaza’s Health Ministry reported receiving a total of 10 bodies over the past 48 hours – nine newly killed and one recovered from under rubble – along with 18 wounded.

It said other victims remain trapped beneath destroyed buildings or on roads that ambulance and civil defence crews have been unable to reach.

Since the “ceasefire” between Israel and Hamas took effect in October last year, the ministry said, 1,313 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli attacks.

Meanwhile, between 4,000 and 5,000 Palestinians remain missing and are believed to be under rubble in Gaza, the Palestinian Centre for Missing and Forcibly Disappeared Persons said on Saturday.

It added that between 2,500 and 3,000 people may have been subjected to forced disappearance in Gaza during Israel’s genocidal war.

The centre’s estimate is based on an analytical study of a sample of 317 cases, and it said the findings showed indicators warranting an investigation into the possibility of a broader pattern of enforced disappearances.

Of the 317 cases examined, 302, or 95.27 percent, were male and 15 were female. The sample included 41 children and 17 people aged 60 or older.

Since Israel’s war began in October 2023, more than 73,000 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza and more than 174,000 injured, most of them women and children.

articles.title: Men are skipping showers before dates for a reason that may surprise women
articles.summary: Pheromone-maxxing has men skipping showers and deodorant before dates, but the science behind natural body odor and attraction remains inconclusive.
articles.body: As if dating weren’t already enough of a gamble, a new trend has some men skipping their usual hygiene routines before meeting a prospective partner. So-called "pheromone-maxxing" is a viral TikTok trend primarily associated with teen boys and young men that involves skipping showers and deodorant before a date. Some proponents go so far as to wear unwashed shirts or drink their own urine in an effort to "sweat out toxins," VICE reported. 'LOOKSMAXXING' TREND HAS YOUNG MEN TAKING HAMMERS TO THEIR FACES IN PURSUIT OF SHARPER FEATURES Pheromones are chemical compounds that transmit signals between members of the same species. They are well documented in insects and other animals, and some pheromones do not have a discernible scent, Scientific American explained. The theory behind pheromone-maxxing is that the stronger a man’s natural musk, the more sexually attractive he is. The scientific evidence behind that idea, however, is inconclusive. Researchers have found evidence that human body odors and secretions can influence physiological or psychological responses in other people. "But there is no evidence of a consistent and strong behavioral response to any human-produced chemical cue," Scientific American reported. "To date, scientists have collected evidence for possible pheromone effects but have not definitively identified a single human pheromone." One of the best-known experiments examining scent and attraction was a 1995 study commonly called the "sweaty t-shirt study." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Male participants wore the same T-shirt for two consecutive nights, after which female participants were asked to rate the odors of six shirts. Women generally rated the body odors of men whose MHC (major histocompatibility complex) genes differed from their own as more pleasant than those of men with more similar MHC genes. The MHC is a group of genes that plays a key role in the immune system and may also influence individual body odor. Among women taking oral contraceptives, however, that preference was reversed. Later research has produced mixed results. A 2019 study of 883 couples found that people from the Netherlands and Northern Europe were more likely to choose partners with different MHC genes. Researchers did not find the same pattern among Israeli couples and suggested a history of arranged marriages in some groups could help explain why. A 2020 analysis of previous studies, however, found no strong evidence that people prefer partners with different MHC genes or find their body odor more attractive. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Pheromone-maxxing is tied to the broader "looksmaxxing" movement, in which social-media users attempt to optimize their appearance and attractiveness, sometimes through extreme measures such as cosmetic procedures and drastic diets. Pheromone-maxxing has been making recent headlines, but the concept has circulated online since at least 2024. A thread that year in the r/TikTokCringe subreddit drew a largely repulsed response. "And how are those natural pheromones helping him in real life human social interactions?" one Redditor wondered. "I am confused," commented another. "Does he think that bathing means you no longer make pheromones? Is nobody able to teach him?" "There’s no way in hell I would let my child go to school or even in my house smelling stinky," another user wrote. "It’s actually sad that no one in his life has taught him the importance of cleanliness." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Discussing the trend on Fox News’ "The Five," co-host Jesse Watters said, "I’m anti-cologne." He recommended a simple pre-date shower with bar soap and shampoo. Panelist Tyrus agreed and urged men to use unscented deodorant. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES "If men put too much cologne on, you’re a creep," he said. "You’re sending the wrong message. You don’t want to smell like gym class, but you also don’t want to smell like you’re cheap."

articles.title: Drug institute warns that Trump-shaped ecstasy pills contain potentially fatal ingredient
articles.summary: The Trimbos Institute in the Netherlands issued a red alert after Donald Trump-shaped ecstasy pills containing potentially fatal PMMA were handed in at testing centers.
articles.body: A respected drug treatment and mental health center in the Netherlands issued a warning against taking ecstasy pills that are shaped like President Donald Trump’s head, saying they could be fatal. The Trimbos Institute warned in a "red alert" that the pills contain a high concentration of PMMA, also known as para-methoxymethamfetamine, which is similar to ecstasy’s active ingredient MDMA, but is slower acting. The slow onset could encourage users to take more and potentially overdose. The institute shared a photo of two of the pills, of which one was green on the front and one was yellow and they were red and blue on the back. POLICE SEIZE COCAINE BRICKS WITH STICKERS OF NORWEGIAN SOCCER STAR ERLING HAALAND ALL OVER THEM The pills had a likeness of Trump’s face on the front and the name "Trump" and letter "NL" on the back. "Absolutely do not use these pills," the institute urged. In 2018, Indiana State police seized orange Trump-shaped ecstasy pills in an operation targeting small-time drug traffickers. Those pills also had Trump’s face on the front and "great again" written on the back, an apparent reference to his Make America Great Again slogan. In 2017, German police also seized thousands of Trump-shaped ecstasy pills, which also appeared to be orange, that had an estimated street value of nearly $46,000. There have yet to be any reports of overdoses or deaths due to the drug, Spokesperson Anniek Groothuis told the Associated Press. GERMAN POLICE SEIZE THOUSANDS OF 'TRUMP' ECSTASY TABLETS "We do not know of any victims where PMMA was found in their blood," she said. The clinic said that the pills had recently been handed in to some of their centers where they test drugs before people take them. The Sunday Telegraph says John Healey is mulling a windfall tax on banks and oil companies in the Budget. Treasury officials are said to be looking at ways of plugging a £4.7bn black hole without raising direct taxes on individuals.

The paper suggests banks and oil companies are seen as "low-hanging fruit". BP is said to have more than doubled its profits between April and June because of higher oil prices driven by the Iran war. In its editorial, the paper warns against the windfall tax move, saying it will harm growth by denting investor confidence.

According to the Mail on Sunday , Russia is poised to target Britain with a cyber attack on a drone or missile factory. A key advisor to President Vladimir Putin, the former deputy foreign minister Andrei Fedorov, tells the paper the highest levels of the Russian government are considering such a strike. A drone factory owned by the British Ukrainian firm, Ukrspecsystems, is said to be a target. Its location, near RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk, was made public in April.

The deal with union leaders was said to have been made to avoid strikes on a flagship service, and one of the busiest lines in Europe. The paper suggests industrial action would have proved embarrassing for cabinet ministers travelling to the prime minister's new political hub, Number 10 North, in Manchester.

According to both the Sunday Telegraph and the Sunday People , new studies suggest statins can reduce the risk of dementia, as well as lowering cholesterol and the risk of heart attacks. The Telegraph reports that the largest study by Denmark's Copenhagen University Hospital found that the daily pills reduced the chances of dementia by up to 15%. The paper says the research means statins could benefit around six million of almost 10 million people aged 70 and over in the UK who are not currently taking them.

The Sunday Mirror reports that Peter Homa, the ex-boss of Nottingham NHS Trust, where a review found that 520 mothers or babies suffered potentially avoidable death or harm, is now CEO of a firm giving maternity training to the health service. articles.title: Acidente na Dutra em São José dos Campos deixa quatro feridos | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu na noite de sábado (29), no km 154, sentido São Paulo. Quatro pessoas ficaram feridas.
articles.summary: Um acidente na Dutra em São José dos Campos, provocado por um carro na contramão, deixou quatro feridos, sendo três em estado grave, na noite de sábado.
articles.body:
Carro na contramão bate de frente com outro veículo e deixa quatro feridos na Dutra, em São José — Foto: Divulgação/PRF

Uma colisão frontal entre dois carros deixou três pessoas gravemente feridas e uma com ferimentos leves na noite deste sábado (29), na Rodovia Presidente Dutra, em São José dos Campos . Segundo a concessionária RioSP, um dos veículos trafegava na contramão.

O acidente aconteceu por volta das 20h30, na altura do km 154, no sentido São Paulo. Equipes da RioSP e do Corpo de Bombeiros foram acionadas para atender a ocorrência e prestar socorro às vítimas.

Ao todo, quatro pessoas ficaram feridas. Três foram classificadas em estado grave e uma teve ferimentos leves.

Uma das vítimas graves era o motorista do veículo que trafegava na contramão. Ele foi levado para a Santa Casa de Jacareí.

As outras duas vítimas em estado grave e a vítima que teve ferimentos leves foram encaminhadas para o Hospital da Vila Industrial, em São José dos Campos.

Durante o atendimento, a pista sentido São Paulo precisou ser totalmente interditada. Depois, o tráfego passou a fluir pela faixa da direita. Segundo a concessionária, não houve registro de congestionamento.

Os veículos envolvidos na colisão foram removidos. As circunstâncias do acidente serão investigadas.

articles.title: Explosão em Santo Antônio de Jesus: morre adolescente de 13 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Talita dos Santos Nascimento, de 14 anos, estava internada Hospital Geral do Estado (HGE) desde 19 de agosto, quando o acidente aconteceu. Informação foi confirmada pela equipe médica.
articles.summary: Talita Nascimento faleceu no HGE após a explosão em Santo Antônio de Jesus, acidente que também vitimou sua mãe e deixou outra criança ferida na Bahia.
articles.body:
Diana Guimarães dos Santos da Silva, de 42 anos, e a filha Talita dos Santos Nascimento, de 14 — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Morreu na noite do sábado (29), em Salvador , a segunda vítima da explosão de gás que atingiu três casas na cidade de Santo Antônio de Jesus , no Recôncavo da Bahia. Talita dos Santos Nascimento , de 14 anos, estava internada Hospital Geral do Estado (HGE) desde 19 de agosto, quando o acidente aconteceu. A informação foi confirmada pela equipe médica.

Na última terça-feira (25), Diana Guimarães, de 42 anos, morreu na mesma unidade de saúde após complicações em um procedimento cirúrgico . Diana era mãe de Talita e teve quase todo o corpo queimado.

No mesmo dia da morte da mãe, Talita teve uma piora no quadro de saúde. Familiares iniciaram uma campanha por doação de sangue para a adolescente, mas a situação se agravou e ela não resistiu.

O corpo da adolescente será velado neste domingo, às 14h, em um centro de velório na cidade de Santo Antônio de Jesus. O sepultamento está previsto para às 16h no Cemitério Municipal.

Uma terceira vítima, identificada como Eloísa Silva Alves, de 9 anos, segue internada no Hospital Regional de Santo Antônio de Jesus.

Conforme apuração da TV Subaé, afiliada da Rede Bahia na região, a garota teve parte do corpo queimado e uma fratura no fêmur. Ela precisou passar por dois procedimentos cirúrgicos desde o ocorrido e segue sob avaliação médica.

Botijão de gás causou explosão e três casas foram atingidas em Santo Antônio de Jesus — Foto: Tino Alves

A explosão aconteceu em uma região de Santo Antônio de Jesus conhecida como Casco. A suspeita inicial é de que ela tenha sido provocada pelo vazamento de um botijão de gás. Segundo a Defesa Civil, um laudo de perícia será realizado para determinar as causas do acidente. Informações iniciais indicam que a mangueira do botijão estava vencida desde 2019.

O Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi acionado por volta das 5h e encaminhou uma das vítimas para o Hospital Regional de Santo Antônio de Jesus (HRSAJ). As outras duas foram socorridas anteriormente por equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros, com apoio de moradores, e também levadas para a unidade de saúde.

Eloísa Silva, de 9 anos, teve queimaduras nas pernas e no rosto, além de uma fratura no fêmur. De acordo com familiares, ela estava passando a noite na casa da amiga, Talita Santos de Andrade, de 13 anos, quando a explosão aconteceu.

Segundo familiares, a mulher morava sozinha com a filha e havia se mudado para o imóvel, que era alugado, há cerca de oito dias. Equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros estiveram no local para atender à ocorrência. A situação das casas vizinhas também deverá ser avaliada.

articles.title: Museu da Loucura: conheça a história do espaço em Barbacena | G1
articles.standfirst: Instalado na estrutura do antigo hospital, o museu preserva a memória de uma das maiores tragédias da saúde mental no país. Visitantes podem conhecer itens e objetos que ajudam a contar a história da instituição.
articles.summary: Instalado em uma estrutura do antigo hospital, espaço preserva a memória de uma das maiores tragédias da saúde mental no país. Visitantes podem conhecer documentos, fotografias e o
articles.body:
Prédio do Museu da Loucura, em Barbacena — Foto: Juliana Netto/g1

O Museu da Loucura funciona dentro do Centro Hospitalar Psiquiátrico de Barbacena (CHPB), na área onde funcionou o Hospital Colônia , considerado o maior manicômio do Brasil, que se tornou símbolo de uma das maiores tragédias humanitárias da história do país.

O acervo reúne objetos originais do Hospital Colônia , além de fotografias, documentos, equipamentos médicos e conteúdos audiovisuais sobre a história da assistência psiquiátrica em Minas Gerais.

As exposições mostram as experiências vividas pelos pacientes ao longo das décadas, no que ficou conhecido como 'Holocausto Brasileiro' . O espaço também funciona como local de memória e reflexão sobre a importância do respeito à dignidade humana no atendimento em saúde mental.

Museu da Loucura guarda fotos e objetos de quem viveu no espaço — Foto: Juliana Netto/g1

Recebe visitantes de diferentes partes do país, incluindo turistas, estudantes, pesquisadores e profissionais da saúde.

Completou 30 anos de existência no d ia 16 de agosto de 2026 e foi o primeiro museu brasileiro dedicado à saúde mental no Brasil.

Criado no início em 1903, o Hospital Colônia recebeu pacientes de diferentes regiões de Minas Gerais e do país. Muitos deles não tinham diagnóstico de transtorno mental, e as internações eram compulsórias e pouco fiscalizadas.

Por isso, também eram levadas para lá pessoas indesejadas pela sociedade da época, como alcoólatras, homossexuais, mendigos, prostitutas, órfãos, opositores políticos e mulheres que haviam perdido a virgindade antes do casamento ou sido rejeitadas pelos maridos.

Imagem de arquivo mostra pacientes do Hospital Colônia de Barbacena — Foto: Divulgação

Houve graves violações de direitos humanos e, dentre as práticas adotadas, estava o uso de eletrochoques como forma de punição por comportamentos considerados indesejados, como chorar, tentar fugir ou não seguir ordens.

Painel que fica no Museu da Loucura, em Barbacena — Foto: Juliana Netto/g1

As descargas eram aplicadas sem anestesia e por funcionários sem qualificação para o procedimento, causando dores intensas e até queimaduras nos pacientes, que dormiam em um modelo conhecido como “leito único”, diretamente no chão frio e cobertos apenas por capim seco.

Diante de tantas atrocidades, o Hospital Colônia ficou conhecido como 'Holocausto Brasileiro'.

Em 25 de maio deste ano, os 14 últimos moradores que permaneciam no hospital foram levados para uma residência terapêutica , onde receberão acompanhamento especializado. Todos são muito idosos e nenhum mantém contato com familiares.

Pelo menos 1.800 corpos de pessoas que morreram no hospital foram vendidos para universidades e usados em aulas de anatomia nas faculdades de medicina.

Museu da Loucura, em Barbacena — Foto: Juliana Netto/g1

O Ministério Público Federal (MPF) também ajuizou uma ação civil pública contra a Fundação Educacional Lucas Machado (Feluma), a Fundação Hospitalar do Estado de Minas Gerais (Fhemig), o Estado de Minas Gerais e a União. O órgão pede reparação histórica pela venda de corpos utilizados em aulas de dissecação na Faculdade de Ciências Médicas de Minas Gerais entre 1971 e 1975.

A ação pede que as instituições sejam condenadas a adotar medidas como o pagamento de R$ 13,7 milhões por danos morais coletivos, a publicação de declarações oficiais e a realização de cerimônias públicas de reconhecimento dos fatos.

O museu fica na avenida 14 de Agosto, no bairro Floresta, dentro do Centro Hospitalar Psiquiátrico de Barbacena. O funcionamento é das 13h às 17h às segundas-feiras e 9h às 17h, entre terça e domingo.

A entrada é gratuita. O espaço recebe turistas, estudantes, pesquisadores e profissionais da saúde de diferentes regiões do Brasil.

Escadaria do Museu da Loucura, em Barbacena — Foto: Juliana Netto/g1

articles.title: Homem é morto a tiros e mulher fica ferida em bar de Boa Vista | G1
articles.standfirst: José Avelino Fernandez Devera, de 27 anos, morreu em um bar no bairro Jóquei Clube, na zona Oeste de Boa Vista.
articles.summary: José Avelino Fernandez Devera, de 27 anos, morreu em um bar no bairro Jóquei Clube, na zona Oeste de Boa Vista.
articles.body:
José Avelino Fernandez Devera — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

José Avelino Fernandez Devera, de 27 anos, foi morto a tiros e uma mulher, de 44 anos, ficou ferida na madrugada deste domingo (29) em um bar , , na zona Oeste de Boa Vista .

De acordo com a Polícia Militar (PM), ele foi encontrado caído com várias perfurações no peito e no abdômen. O suspeito não foi identificado .

À PM, a mulher ferida contou que estava no bar com amigos quando ouviu os disparos. Em seguida, percebeu que havia sido baleada no braço esquerdo. Ela foi levada ao Hospital Geral de Roraima (HGR).

Uma equipe do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi chamada ao bar e confirmou a morte de José ainda no local.

A PM fez buscas para tentar identificar e localizar o responsável pelo crime. Os policiais também obtiveram imagens das câmeras de segurança do estabelecimento para ajudar nas investigações.

A área foi isolada para preservar vestígios. Equipes da perícia e da Polícia Civil estiveram no local. O corpo de José foi removido para o Instituto Médico Legal (IML).

articles.title: North Carolina warns mobile petting zoo visitors of rabies exposure after baby goats test positive
articles.summary: Baby goats at Farm Adventures, a North Carolina mobile petting zoo, tested positive for rabies after a skunk entered their pen and bit them.
articles.body: North Carolina health officials are urging people who touched baby goats at a mobile petting zoo to contact their local health department after several goats tested positive for rabies. The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (NCDHHS) said the infected goats were from Farm Adventures, a mobile petting zoo based in Harmony, North Carolina, that attended off-site events across multiple counties. Anyone who had contact with baby goats from Farm Adventures, either at its Harmony location or at an off-site event between July 28 and Aug. 27, should contact their local health department to determine whether medication is needed to prevent infection, according to NCDHHS. RABID BAT FOUND NEAR ZOO RESTAURANT SPARKS URGENT PUBLIC HEALTH WARNING: 'EXTREMELY SERIOUS' During that period, NCDHHS said Farm Adventures held off-site events involving children and elderly individuals across multiple counties. Organizers of those events are being notified, the agency said, adding that the investigation remains ongoing and additional information about potential exposure locations will be released when available. In a Facebook statement, Farm Adventures said four of its baby goats had contracted rabies and that the animals had been euthanized to prevent further spread. MARYLAND ROCKED BY THIRD BEAVER ATTACK IN WEEKS AFTER 2 ANIMALS TEST POSITIVE FOR RABIES The petting zoo identified the goats as Molly, Maggie, Cow and Uno. "We are working closely with public health officials, the North Carolina Department of Agriculture, and animal control to address this issue and ensure the safety of our animals and clients," Farm Adventures said. According to Farm Adventures, the baby goats were housed in a separate pen away from the other animals at the petting zoo. The four goats were too young to receive their vaccinations when a skunk entered their pen, according to Farm Adventures. While the skunk was removed, the petting zoo was not aware that the goats had been bitten. "They showed no sign or symptoms of rabies," Farm Adventures said. DEADLIEST ANIMAL IN EVERY US STATE REVEALED, FROM MOOSE AND BEARS TO DOGS Farm Adventures said one of the animals was ultimately sent for a necropsy after its veterinarian investigated what was happening. State health officials said several goats tested positive for rabies at the North Carolina State Laboratory of Public Health. "These past few days have been incredibly difficult for us," Farm Adventures said. Rabies is a viral disease that is deadly if people do not receive medical care before symptoms begin, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The virus primarily spreads through bites or scratches from an infected animal. Bats, skunks, raccoons and foxes are the animals most frequently found with rabies in the U.S., according to the CDC. The CDC said roughly 100,000 Americans receive rabies vaccinations following a potential exposure each year. articles.title: Why Dolly Parton’s death can feel like losing someone you knew personally
articles.summary: Fans worldwide describe "post-Parton depression" as Dolly Parton's death triggers intense parasocial grief that psychologists say mirrors real loss.
articles.body: The death of Dolly Parton has prompted an outpouring of grief from fans around the world, many of whom have shared that they feel like they’ve lost someone they knew personally. Grief experts say it’s possible to experience genuine feelings of loss even if there wasn’t a personal relationship — particularly when the public figure has become woven into people’s memories and routines over a long period of time. Psychologists refer to this type of loss as parasocial grief, according to licensed clinical psychologist Dr. Dara Houp. DOLLY PARTON’S PRIVATE CANCER BATTLE HIGHLIGHTS WHY SOME PATIENTS DON’T SHARE THEIR DIAGNOSES "When a celebrity shares their personal life – childhood experiences, hardships and victories – our brains register these bits of information through the same emotional and neural pathways utilized for our real-life friendships and a genuine attachment is developed," Houp, with Pathways Psychological Services in New York City, told Fox News Digital. When that perceived relationship comes to an end, people may experience the parasocial grief, she said. Desiree Taranto, a licensed mental health counselor and clinical director at Empower Your Mind Therapy in New York City, said the widespread reaction also reflects "collective grief," a shared emotional response when a loss resonates across a community. "Parton’s music, movies, philanthropy and public persona became part of many people’s family traditions, memories and difficult life moments," she told Fox News Digital. Fans share their grief "I honestly didn’t know I could react that way over someone I don’t even personally know," one user wrote in a grief support group on Reddit. "[Dolly] was a ray of sunshine in this dark world nowadays, and I just can’t help but cry and get so emotional about it." Another user shared that "as each day passes, losing Dolly seems to hurt more instead of less. I have found myself crying and feeling this deep sadness that I just can’t shake." IN WAKE OF DOLLY PARTON'S DEATH, ONCOLOGIST REVEALS WHY SOME PATIENTS KEEP CANCER DIAGNOSES SECRET "I never met Dolly, and I know she didn’t know me, but I loved her for most of my life. That love was real, and so this grief feels real too." Someone else in a different group referred to the feelings of sadness as "post-Parton depression." "I don't know why I am taking Dolly Parton's death so hard," one user wrote. "I never met her… She didn't know me. But for some reason, I can't stop crying." "I think the reason it's hard is because she was a light and just a wonderful human," someone else shared. "She is exactly who Jesus wanted us to be." Why does it feel personal? The emotions people experience when grieving a celebrity can feel as real as those felt after losing someone they knew personally, Houp said. "Perceived relational intimacy, not whether we actually know an individual, is largely what determines the intensity of grief," she said. "The emotional connection your brain developed runs along the same neural pathways as real-life bonds." "Accept your feelings and know that it is okay to mourn someone you never met." It’s also possible that the deaths of certain celebrities — particularly those associated with childhood, family traditions or major life moments — are more likely to trigger an intense grief response, the expert noted. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "When a celebrity’s life is connected to a personal milestone — such as a break-up or the birth of a child — their death permanently disrupts a living connection to who, what or where you used to be," Houp said. "Losing a celebrity can feel like losing a piece of your own history." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A song may be tied to someone who has died, a family memory or a difficult period when Parton’s work brought comfort, Taranto noted, making the loss feel connected to a person’s own life story. Over decades in the public eye, Parton gave fans a window into her life, allowing them to form a sense of who she was, Houp said. "For many who followed Dolly’s life, she represented resilience and ambition, authenticity and bold self-expression, and a rare, unconditional kindness," she said. "We identified with the goodness we saw in Dolly and felt encouraged by her ability to overcome hardship – thereby furthering our sense of connection to her." Tips to navigate grief Taranto offered advice for those feeling the grief following Parton’s death. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "Accept your feelings and know that it is okay to mourn someone you never met," she said. "Do not judge yourself or feel embarrassed because that person’s work, values or advocacy touched your life personally." It can also help to reach out to others who are also grieving the loss. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Be there for each other and allow others to be there for you," Taranto advised. "Tell stories, listen to her music, watch her movies or journal about what she meant to you." "Remember the positive impact she made in the world and the ways she used her platform for good. Shared grief can help us process a loss because it reminds us that we are not alone in it."
